Options that bound the work of a search or a fit

Source: R/spatialkit-topics.R
spatialkit-options.Rd

The package reads two options. Each bounds a step whose cost grows with the square of the rows or of the cells, so that such a step stops, or is skipped, before it starts. Set them with options().

The options

spatialkit.exact_pairs_max

Default 2e9 pairs. The most pairs a search made without the FNN package may compare. Without FNN, a nearest-neighbour search (each cell's neighbours, each row's nearest centre, each location's nearest other location) compares every pair, and a search over the pairs of about 44,700 cells or locations reaches the default. With FNN, which installs with spatialkit, these searches use a kd-tree and the limit is not read. The result of every search is the same with and without FNN. Above the limit:

  • resolution_profile() stops with an error of class spatialkit_work_limit before the search: on a ladder of sizes, for the weights of partition = "density"; with an estimate, on any ladder, for the estimate's searches.

  • cell_values_at() stops with the same error before the search.

  • summarize_by_cell() returns NA pooled columns with a warning of class spatialkit_pool_unavailable (reason = "work limit"), and does not run the check of the count record ("not checked: work limit").

  • select_resolution() hands on the centres fitted to the subsample without refitting them to every point, with a logged warning.

spatialkit.fit_work_max

Default 1e10 point-to-centre comparisons. The most work the partition fits of a ladder of sizes may do: the points times the cells of the finest level times nstart, times iter_max for partition = "density" without FNN. With FNN and init = "random" the density kind has no step that compares every point with every centre, and nothing is counted. Above the limit, resolution_profile() stops with an error of class spatialkit_work_limit before any fit. At the default size the work grows with the square of the rows. select_resolution() refits the centres of a profile fitted to a subsample to every point, and counts the points times the cells of the count it selects, times iter_max for the density kind without FNN, whatever the start. Above the limit it hands on the centres fitted to the subsample, with a logged warning.

Setting a limit

Each option takes a single number, 0 or more; Inf removes the limit. Any other value is an error when the option is read. The error of class spatialkit_work_limit carries work (the count), limit and what (the step), and its message says what to change: for a fit, fewer starts, a coarser obs_per_cell, random starts of the density kind or a higher limit; for a search, reinstalling FNN. A profile just below spatialkit.fit_work_max prints nothing while its fits run.

The console log is set with spatialkit_quiet(), not with an option.

See also

spatialkit-conditions for the classes named here, and resolution_profile() for the work its fits do.

Other options and caches: clear_fitted_cache(), clear_grid_cache(), spatialkit-conditions, spatialkit_quiet()

Examples

getOption("spatialkit.exact_pairs_max", 2e9)
#> [1] 2e+09
getOption("spatialkit.fit_work_max", 1e10)
#> [1] 1e+10

# Raise one limit for a session, then put it back.
old <- options(spatialkit.fit_work_max = 2e10)
getOption("spatialkit.fit_work_max")
#> [1] 2e+10
options(old)
